From my perspective, as someone only interested in Modern, Legacy, and Vintage:

This set is dull. I play Merfolk, and I was hoping for some new dudes to tinker with. There are two mono-blue Merfolk. Two. And they suck.

Flipping through the spoiler, some high/lowlights

Bane of Bala Ged: Actually kind of cool. Possibly a Tron add in? If it were common, I'd absolutely play it in Pauper Tron.

Breaker of Armies: See above.

Desolation Twin: Broodmate Eldrazi is funny, but I'm not sure how much of a splash it will make in any format.

Kozilek's Channeler: "Our market research told us that players LOVE Sunastian Falconer and Princess Lucrezia, so we designed this card to appeal to those players."

Scour From Existence: Oh, fuck off WotC.

Ulamog, the Ceaseless Hunger: I'll just learn from last time and hold on to any I pull...

Void Winnower: Is weird. I appreciate weird.

Emeria Shepherd: Neat, but likely too high of a casting cost to impact Standard, much less anywhere else.

Gideon, Ally of Zendikar: Is a Gideon. Next.

Lithomancer's Focus: That is going to be hilarious in Limited. Likely won't see play outside of that.

Quarantine Field: I misread this at first, and thought it put counters that were removed, and when all the counters were removed, the permanent would come back. That was awful. Then I reread it. It's still awful.

Smite the Monstrous: I can't take this seriously because I've been playing since 1995, and Reprisal is a card that exists.

Stasis Snare: One of the best cards in the set in my opinion, if only due to Flash. I love it.

Brilliant Spectrum: Reanimator/Dredge/Delve/Shenanigans will occur due to this card. Sorcery hurts, but I think it's a solid card.

Guardian of Tazeem: I so want this card to be good, because it's an awesome old-school control card. Sadly, WotC doesn't allow for that style of play anymore, because they're the fun police.

Horribly Awry: More poopy counterspells, yay!

Retreat to Coralhelm: Knight of the Reliquary shenanigans not withstanding, I tried to fit this into Merfolk and it's just not a thing. Riding the fence on this one. The combo with Knight is cute, but....eh.

Roilmage's Trick: I think at this point it's safe to say that Converge mostly sucks.

(I'm quickly losing interest because this set is boring)

Ugin's Insight: Tutor for three if you have a big enough dude. Not the worst thing, but at five to cast, it's almost a Time Walk for your opponent.

Carrier Thrall: Not the worst thing. Neat in Aristocrats decks. I kind of like it actually.

Drana, Liberator of Malakir: Uh...at least it says "every creature" not "every other". I can't help comparing it to Vampire Nighthawk, and Nighthawk wins just due to not being Legendary.

Hagra Sharpshooter: Pay a billion mana, kill a 1/1.

Ob Nixilis, the Who Actually Cares About This Card:

Painful Truths: Another one of the best cards in the set. Rock/Jund lists will very likely use this to max effect. It's pretty great.

Ruinous Path: Because half decent removal has to be rare now because reasons.

Zulaport Cutthroat: Blood Artist 5-8 for Aristocrats decks. More bad flavor text.

Akoum Firebird: Since it has to attack, I wish the phoenix ability was less to use. I personally would skip it.

Barrage Tyrant: The art is funny.

Crumble to Dust: Screw you, Tron.

Makindi Sliderunner: I'm by no means a Limited expert. I'm not even interested in it really. This dude seems like he'll do work in the format though, and I really like him.

Radiant Flames: With the mana fixing from Khans block, this is bound to see Standard play. I doubt it will make a splash beyond that though.

Retreat to Valakut: I like this one. I played Teetering Peaks a lot in the prior Zendikar, and the Falter ability is solid too.

Turn Against: Woo, another Threaten effect. Just imagine the music from your favorite FPS and move on.

Valakut Predator: I'd rather have Lynx or Plated Geopede. That deck was fun.

Beastcaller Savant: Your mana dorks are now two to cast, conditional, and rare.

Blisterpod: Two blockers, or one shot ramp, or more ammo for a Aristocrats deck. I really like this card.

Brood Monitor: DUDES! TONS OF DUDES! ALL OF THE DUDES! This card is crazy and I love it.

Lifespring Druid: Hey, remember when this was just Birds of Paradise? Me too, and now I am sad.

Natural Connection: Hard for me to judge. I want to say playing it at end of opponents turn is going to be sweet, but how often will a green deck be sitting on that mana? Smarter people than me can handle this one.

Plated Crusher: Big dumb dudes are funny.

Sylvan Scrying: YAY! No more paying five freaking dollars for this card.

Tajuru Stalwart: A possible 3/4 for three isn't something to get excited about anymore.

Undergrowth Champion: A creature with the phantom ability that can regrow the counters is totally worth looking into. Nice card.

Bring to Light: Possibly hilarious in decks that are built to utilize Cascade, as a backup utility. Tutoring up and casting those Time Spiral homage suspend cards is some good.

Brutal Expulsion: Is awesome. Next.

Kiora, Master of Depths: The +1 can essentially make her 2 to cast with the right setup. I like her far better than old Kiora, and I even liked that one. One of the top cards in the set, easily. She ramps, tutors, and dumps stuff in the graveyard, and you will never see that hilarious ultimate.

Noyan Dar, Roil Shaper: Is so silly that I love it. I doubt it's going to be a major player, but it could be a fun casual build around card.

Blighted Woodland: Even the best one of the bunch is still worse than just playing Evolving Wilds.

Canopy Vista, etc: They're fetchable. They'll be fine in Standard I'm sure, but I don't see any use past that.

Lumbering Falls: Interesting, but very hard for me to evaluate. Four mana to activate is a lot, but Hexproof can end up being a corner case that will protect it from things like Ghost Quarter.

Noah Bradley Basics: Holy crap, those are awesome.
